# cursor-click-to-move (on by default): a plain click in the command being
# typed moves the shell's cursor there; the shell's own line editor does it,
# from the arrow keys Libertty presses (so what's typed next lands there).
# (zsh's print -z puts the command with its CJK in the line editor.)
type:print -z "echo abc$(printf '\344\270\255\346\226\207')xyz"
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect:echo abc中文xyz
click-text:中文
type:-
key:enter
expect:abc-中文xyz
# Back to the start, then past the end: after its last character.
type:echo one two
click-text:one
type:X
click-text:two+10
type:!
key:enter
expect:Xone two!
# Not while a program runs: cat gets no arrows.
type:cat -v
key:enter
wait:0.3
type:hello
click-text:hel
type:Z
key:enter
expect:helloZ
expect-not:^[[
key:ctrl+c
